verdict: Verisign grew revenue 5.7% to $443M as the domain name base expanded 6.1%, and kept $213M — about 48 cents of every revenue dollar — as profit.

kpis.label: Operating margin
kpis.note: $296M of operating income on $443M of revenue

segments.name: Domain name registry services
segments.note: Verisign runs the authoritative registry for .com and .net — every registration and renewal worldwide pays it a wholesale fee. It reports a single segment. The domain base grew by 3.36M names in the quarter to 182.5M.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building and securing the registry infrastructure, including the new .web launch and the Verisign Informed validation service.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs — running a very lean operation.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $21M on the company's senior notes, partly offset by $4M of non-operating income.

takeaways.title: The domain base is growing again
takeaways.text: The .com and .net base reached 182.5M names, up 6.1% YoY, with 13.1M new registrations processed in the quarter versus 10.6M a year ago.

takeaways.title: A registry is a toll booth
takeaways.text: Operating income was $296M on $443M of revenue — a 67% margin. Running the registry costs little; most of each renewal fee drops through to profit.

takeaways.title: Profits go back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Verisign repurchased 0.7M shares for $189M in the quarter and declared a $0.81 per share dividend, payable November 24, 2026.

oneTimers: A $7.5M pre-tax operating loss related to certain assets held for sale, which reduced diluted EPS by $0.06.
